The linked reports have different stacktraces so they're likely not the same issue.

Crashes like this are often caused by GPU driver bugs on old devices, so indeed using the Mobile renderer on Android 10 (though theoretically supported) can cause this kind of problems.

To have better logs, you'd need to compile your own export templates with debug symbols to upload to Google Play (the Google console strips the debug symbols automatically, but keeps them to symbolicate the stacktraces they report to you).

See instructions in https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/contributing/development/compiling/compiling_for_android.html regarding adding `debug_symbols=yes` for builds. Note that this works with 4.5 / `master` branch, for 4.1 it's possible too but less easy and not properly documented. Maybe @godotengine/android can help there.

-According to Claude..

The sequence is:
The app is being terminated (_terminate → Main::cleanup)
During cleanup, AudioServer is tearing down its stream playback list
It tries to delete an AudioStreamPlaybackMicrophone node
The destructor calls is_playing() on the microphone playback while it's being destroyed
is_playing() ends up calling AudioDriverOpenSL::input_stop()
SIGSEGV at line 295 — the recorder SLObjectItf pointer is already null or dangling

Line 295 is exactly (*recorder)->Destroy(recorder) — it's trying to destroy an OpenSL recorder object that's already been destroyed or invalidated.

Godot's Main::cleanup() panics, starts tearing down the audio drivers,
and then trips over the "ghost" of the microphone, resulting in a use-after-free SIGSEGV.

I can reproduce the `GodotVulkanRenderView.lambda$onActivityResumed$1` / `VkThread.run` crash deterministically on Godot 4.6.1.

### Environment

- Godot `4.6.1.stable.official.14d19694e`
- Samsung Galaxy Z Fold3 (`SM-F926N`)
- Android 15, arm64
- Qualcomm / Adreno
- Mobile renderer (Vulkan)

### Trigger

The crash occurs when a force-stopped Godot activity is started through ADB while the display remains asleep:

```sh
adb shell am force-stop "$PACKAGE"
adb shell input keyevent KEYCODE_SLEEP
adb shell dumpsys power | grep 'mWakefulness=Asleep'
adb shell am start -W -n "$PACKAGE/$LAUNCHER_ACTIVITY"
```

This reproduced twice out of two attempts. Both processes crashed after an uptime of 3 seconds. Waking the device, dismissing keyguard, and waiting for `mWakefulness=Awake` before `am start` avoids the crash in repeated launches.

A limited Compatibility renderer probe did not produce this `VkThread` crash, but it was not a valid functional control because that launch stalled before the Godot main loop.

### Tombstone signature

Two retained Android tombstones at `2026-07-17 02:08:49 +0900` and `02:11:52 +0900` have the same signature:

```text
ABI: 'arm64'
Process uptime: 3s
name: VkThread
signal 11 (SIGSEGV), code 1 (SEGV_MAPERR)
fault addr 0x0000000000000218
Cause: null pointer dereference

#00 libgodot_android.so
#01 libgodot_android.so
#02 libgodot_android.so
#03 libgodot_android.so
#09 org.godotengine.godot.GodotVulkanRenderView.lambda$onActivityResumed$1
#14 org.godotengine.godot.GodotVulkanRenderView.$r8$lambda$...
#19 org.godotengine.godot.GodotVulkanRenderView$$ExternalSyntheticLambda1.run
#24 org.godotengine.godot.vulkan.VkThread.run
```

This looks related to the Vulkan Android resume lifecycle. Issue #89069 may also be relevant because it documents duplicate Vulkan pause/resume delivery, although it does not report this crash.
